title: Ignite 2026: Windows Hello event logs and passwordless updates
summary: Microsoft listed Windows sign-in changes aimed at passwordless rollouts. In the Windows 11 Insider Experimental channel today: Windows Hello sign-in changes (PIN offered alongside Face or Fingerprint, PIN first after a restart), new Windows Hello event logs (HelloForBusiness/Operational and the Security log) that show whether a device was unlocked with Face, Fingerprint or PIN, web sign-in for Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices, and IAKerb. Coming in the November 2026 non-security preview update: an automatic screen-brightness option for face sign-in and an NFC tap location indicator. Coming to Insiders this month: passkey security key management, a Security page in Settings, remote lock, BitLocker TPM + PIN for standard users (Intune-managed) and the Pluton key storage provider.
why: The event logs give you evidence of how users actually sign in, which helps audits and help desk troubleshooting. 'PIN first after restart' changes what users see every morning, so it needs communication before it reaches production. Web sign-in for hybrid joined devices removes a blocker for shared and frontline devices.
todo: Do now: if you run Insider devices, collect the new Windows Hello event logs in a pilot and decide which events to forward to your SIEM.
Prepare user communication for the PIN-first behaviour after restart.
Wait: most items are Insider Experimental channel or 'coming soon'. Announced, not verified on retail builds; watch the Windows release health page and Message Center.
effective_note: Insider Experimental channel today; some items in the November 2026 non-security preview update.
